row.evidence: Dashlane's pricing page says Omnix Password Management costs $8 per user per month billed annually and lists "Integrate with SSO, SCIM, & more"; the plan comparison marks SCIM provisioning as included in Password Management and Enterprise.
row.notes: Status changed gated -> free. Dashlane now sells only Omnix plans (Starter, Team and Standard are no longer sold). Password Management ($8/u/mo annual), the entry password-manager plan, includes SAML SSO and SCIM with no upcharge, so under the price-gate rule this is free (June's own row already had multiplier 1.0). Omnix Credential Protection ($4/u/mo) is a separate phishing/credential-risk product without a vault; the comparison table says it lacks SSO/SCIM while two help articles say otherwise. Enterprise is custom for 50+ users. SCIM no longer needs SSO; documented for Okta, Entra, JumpCloud and PingID; Google Workspace is SSO + JIT only. Group push is off under Confidential SCIM. Public API is read-only.

plans.name: Omnix Credential Protection
plans.notes: Separate credential-risk/phishing product without a vault. The plan comparison marks SSO and SCIM as not included, but two help articles say SSO and SCIM are available with Credential Protection (see conflicts).

plans.name: Omnix Enterprise
plans.price_text: Custom, volume-optimized pricing (Contact Sales); for more than 50 users

auth.token_source: Admin Console > Integrations > Provisioning > Start setup > Generate SCIM API token

operations.notes: Okta guide: Create Users, Update User Attributes, Deactivate Users; Push Groups off. Groups sync via SAML group attribute instead (Confidential); self-hosted SCIM supported group provisioning.

deprovision.data_retained: SSO members removed from the plan permanently lose access to their account and personal data; admins can reactivate a removed member, and can re-add within 30 days to reach work logins.
deprovision.notes: Manual removal frees the license (c29); docs do not say this explicitly for SCIM deactivation.

limitations.text: Group provisioning via Confidential SCIM must be turned off (sharing group creation not supported); groups sync through SAML group attributes instead.
Google Workspace, AD FS and Duo are SSO only; SCIM is not supported for them.
Self-hosted SSO and SCIM can no longer be set up after October 2025.
Groups created in Dashlane do not merge or sync with SCIM groups.

scim.notes: SCIM endpoint URL is shown in the Admin Console (Integrations > Provisioning); its pattern is not published. Confidential SCIM is the only option for new setups; self-hosted (encryption service) SCIM is legacy.

auth.notes: Bearer DLP_ token created in Admin Console > Integrations > Developer Access or via the Dashlane CLI; keys do not expire.

endpoints.purpose: List team members (status, joined date) with paging
Team status: seats, SSO configuration, domains

audit_log_api.notes: Public API has no log endpoints; activity logs go to SIEM integrations instead.

rate_limits.text: Members endpoint returns at most 100 results per page.

limitations.text: Public API is read-only and has no logs, group sharing or vault endpoints.

user_api.notes: Read-only public API (members, devices, password health, team status). No write endpoints for users or groups.

okta.notes: OIN page marks only SAML as checked (read from page markup). Dashlane's guide provisions by enabling SCIM on the Dashlane SAML app with the Dashlane SCIM base URL and token.

entra.notes: Dashlane's guide uses a non-gallery app ('Integrate any other application you don't find in the gallery'); no Entra Learn tutorial found (404).

google.notes: Custom SAML app in Google Workspace; SCIM not supported, JIT recommended.

jumpcloud.notes: JumpCloud's guide lists the Dashlane Encryption service as a prerequisite (self-hosted setup).

fallbacks.other_sync: SAML group sync (Google Workspace); legacy AD sync discontinued
